2  This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e cour  following:
 ORDER Heard on I.A. No.11015/2023, an application seeking permission to amend the valuation and accordingly to pay Court fee.

Learned counsel for the claimants submits that he has paid deficit Court fee of Rs.5,62,500/-
(Rupees Sixty Two Thousand Five Hundred Only)and in support of the said submission he has filed a copy of Online Court Fee Cyber Receipt along with the application, therefore, the Court fee may be taken on record.
On due consideration, I.A. No.11015/2023 is allowed and deficit Court fee is taken on record.

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is filed by the claimants being aggrieved of the award dated 21.11.2013 passed by learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal in MCC No. 2667 of 2012.

It is submitted that the deceased Sudhir Soni had met with an accident on 09.03.2012 he was traveling on his motorcycle at about 04:00 p.m. when he was hit by a motorcycle bearing Registration No. MP-41MJ-7057 owned by respondent No.2 and insured by respondent No.3.

It is submitted that due to accident deceased suffered multiple injuries including fracture of Spine D-6 and D-7 resulting in Paraplegia as is certified by the treating hospital i.e Narmada Health Group vide Ex.P-9.
It is submitted that deceased was admitted in said hospital on 10.03.2012 and was operated on 17.03.2012.
He was operated under General Anesthesia and Open Ruction with Internal fixation of D-4, D-5, D-8 & D-9 was carried out with screw with rods.
Thus, it is submitted that it is not in dispute that deceased was a victim of road transport accident and had sustained injuries on account of road transport accident.
Papers of treatment are available on record.
Deceased was an income-tax payee and his Income-tax return Ex.P-60, P-61 & P-62 for the assessment year, 2009-10, 2011-12 and 2010-11 are available on record.
H e died because of the injuries caused in the accident occurred on 09.11.2012.

It is submitted that concerned Officer from the Income-tax Department namely Ashutosh Chaterjee, Income Tax Inspector was examined as PW-3 and he certified the income for the year, 2009-10 as Rs.1,54,000/-, 2010-11 as Rs.1,70,000/- and year 2011-12 as Rs.1,80,000/-.
Similarly Dr. Ravish Sarraf Medical Officer, Government Hamidiya Medical Hospital, Bhopal was examined as PW-4 and he deposed that the death was due to the injuries which were caused in the accident.

Yet overlooking this vital piece of evidence, learned claims Tribunal has rejected the claim petition in an arbitrary Smt. Krishna vs Pappu on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11762067/
2 and illegal manner overlooking the fact that no independent evidence was lead either by the respondents or by the Insurance Company to dispute lake of co-relation between the cause of accident and the death of deceased.

Shri Sachin Soni, learned counsel for respondent No.1 & 2 and Ms. Anjali Banerjee, learned counsel for respondent No.3 supports the impugned award and submits that there is no nexus between cause of death and the injuries sustained by the deceased, therefore, impugned award be not disturbed.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the records, it is evident that the certain facts have been overlooked by the learned Claims Tribunal..

Deceased Sudhir Soni was admitted in Hamidia Hospital, Bhopal with history of unconsciousness for eight days in a critical condition where he was shifted from a private hospital and kept on a ventilator on inotropic support.
He was subsequently referred to Hamidia Hospital, Bhopal in average critical conditions with fracture of D8-9 Pedicle screw-8 with infected bed sores, no history of DM/HTN/CAD/COPD.

It is mentioned in the prescription ExP-5 that it was an operative case of Traumatic Paraplegia with UTI complicated with bed sore grade (4) with Sepsis with Septic Encephalopathy with respiratory failure with septic shock and eventually he breathed his last on 09.11.2012 of such conditions.
Two facts emerge, whether he is entitled to compensation on account of death or he is to be compensated treating it to be a case of injury.
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has exhaustively argued that there was no postmortem.
This aspect has been dealt with by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Afsana and Ors. Vs.
M / S Kundu
Knit Fab
. Private Ltd.

Though the Director, Krishan Kumar and Anr. in Civil Appeal No.6317 of 2021 arising out of SLP (C) No.5474 of 2018 where facts were that on 05.07.2021 Afsar Ali as a driver of the motorcycle and Kabil as a pillion rider met with an accident with Car No.PB-10AB-5351 resulting in multiple injuries to Afsar Ali as a result of which she lost life.
Kabil suffer serious injuries became quadriplegic and died on 15.08.2002.
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal had granted compensation of payment of medical expenses.

High court in Appeal enhanced compensation by Rs.2,,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lacs Only) on account of the injuries received by Kabil, holding that the appellants have not proved that the death was on account of injuries received.
Hon'ble Supreme Court noticed that Kabil had received serious injuries in the accident and was on bed being a quadriplegic patient.
Death was on account of injuries suffered by him.

Motor Accident Claims Tribunal erred in law to decline amendment of the claim petition and also the fact that injured had remained admitted in his Hospital for more than three months and remained under treatment for a very long time.
He had developed quadriplegia.

A person who is confined to bed and suffering from quadriplegia, the death on 15.08.2002 cannot be for any other reason but on account of injuries suffered by him and, therefore, computed compensation on the principles laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Pranay Sethi and Ors.

3
Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that High Court failed to recording a finding of death on account of injuries.
When the present case is examined, facts are on a better footing.

Accident took place on 09.03.2012, death in November, 2012 i.e. within 9 months of the accident whereas in case of Afsana and Others (supra) death had taken place after more than a year inasmuch as accident was on 05.07.2001 and death had occurred on 15.08.2002.

Another similarity is in that case, deceased had become quadriplegic whereas in the present case there is a medical evidence to suggest that deceased on account of the injuries to the backbone had become Paraplegic.
Paraplegia can occur after a spinal code injury.
It's caused by damage to the Vertebrae, ligaments or disc of the spinal column.
It is a condition which can't be cured.
It effect all the parts of Torso leg and Pelvic organs.

When examined from this aspect then death of Sudhir Soni cannot be said to be not on account of accident though certified by treating doctors and also by the concerned Doctor from Hamidia Hospital, who was examined before the learned Tribunal namely Dr. Ravish Saraf,

therefore, this Court is of the opinion that document, Ex.P-8, which is discharge card of Shri Sudhir Soni and then documents from the Gandhi Medical College, Bhopal which are part of Ex.P- 68-C could not have been overlooked by the learned Tribunal while determining the compensation.
It is mentioned in the claim petition itself that he was working as Civil Foreman in Welspun Projects Ltd. and was drawing salary of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Salary certificate is available on record as Ex.P-7, certifying his salary at Rs.15,000/- per month as basic salary and Rs.3000/- HRA and other Allowances.

Thus, salary of the deceased can be taken at Rs.15,000/- per month or Rs.1,80,000/-
per annum.
1/3rd is to be deducted towards the living expenses of the deceased as he survived by three legal heirs namely his wife and two minor children.

Age of the deceased has come on record as 35 years, therefore, 50% is to be added towards the future prospect and when multiplier of 16 will be applicable, then pecuniary compensation comes to Rs.28,80,000/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lacs Eighty Thousand Only).

In addition thereto Rs.70,000/- (Rupees Seventy Thousand Only) will be added under the head of non- pecuniary compensation and Rs.80,000/- (Rupees Eighty Thousand Only) under the head of loss of love and affection to the children

, then total compensation will come out to Rs.30,30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Lacs Thirty Thousand Only) against a sum of Rs.1,32,960/- (Rupees One Lacs Thirty Two Thousand Nine Hundred and Sixty Only) awarded by learned Claims Tribunal.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.28,97,040/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lacs Ninety Seven Thousand Fourty Only).
This additional amount will also earn interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
This additional amount shall remain invested in a Monthly Income Scheme of an Indian Post Office or Nationalized Bank for a period of ten years.
Claimants will be entitled to use interest so derived for their upkeep and well being, but they will keep the principal amount intact.
In above terms, this miscellaneous appeal is disposed of.
Record of the Tribunal be sent back immediately.
